title: War-room prep: Helios Retail checkout outage - 2026-04-15
content:
Context:
- Helios Retail reported intermittent 500s on /checkout API starting 2026-04-15 08:12 PT. Customer impact: failed checkouts for ~25% of users in NA region, spike correlates with a promo run.
- They escalated to CS at 08:35. Oncall routed to eng-sre and platform. We agreed to war-room at 09:00 PT.

Meeting goals (prep):
- Align on scope and severity (confirm P1).
- Quick timeline of user impact and detection.
- Immediate mitigations to reduce customer pain (workarounds / fallbacks).
- Hypotheses + data queries to validate.
- Assign owners for short-term fix and customer comms.
- Decide post-mortem and next steps.

Agenda (09:00 - 09:45 PT):
1) Quick roll-call and objective (Asha) - 5m
2) Incident timeline summary (Mei) - 5m
3) Live metrics & current state: error rate, latency, capacity (Liam) - 8m
4) Hypotheses and evidence needed (Jordan) - 8m
5) Immediate mitigations (Priya) - 8m
6) Customer comms + CS plan (Asha/Priya) - 6m
7) Action items and owners (everyone) - 5m
8) Wrap & next sync (Asha) - 5m

Current facts / observations:
- First alert: 08:12 PT (SLO error budget exceeded).
- Error type: HTTP 500 with stacktrace pointing at model-routing layer -> downstream model instance returning OOM in logs.
- Affected region: us-west1 and us-east1; us-central unaffected.
- Traffic pattern: sudden spike at 08:10 due to marketing promo; request size slightly larger (avg tokens +15%).
- Autoscaler logs: several dedicated pods reported scale-up throttles between 08:12-08:20.
- Cached prefix hit-rate dropped (cache evictions high) around the same time.

Initial hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
A) Sudden traffic spike with larger sequences caused memory pressure on certain model variants => OOMs and 500s.
B) Kernel/quantization mismatch for the deployed model variant interacting badly with specific input shapes -> degraded perf and errors.
C) Control-plane routing bug misdirecting requests to incompatible instance types under burst => errors.

Data queries to run (priority):
- Query error logs by instance id and model variant from 08:00-09:00 (Liam) -> find OOM indicators.
- Compare token distribution (seq len) for failed vs successful requests (Mei) -> validate larger input sizes.
- Check autoscaler events and failed scale attempts (Jordan) -> confirm throttles.
- Cache eviction timeline correlated with errors (Priya) -> confirm cache pressure.

Immediate mitigations (proposed):
- Short-term: throttle or reject requests above 1.5x median seq length for Helios account (config change) -> reduces pressure (owner: Mei, ETA: 30m).
- Short-term: fallback routing policy to route Helios traffic to model variant B (more stable, lower memory) for next 2 hours (owner: Jordan, ETA: 15m to flip).
- Short-term: temporarily increase dedicated pool for Hosted tier for Helios (reserved burst) to absorb spike (owner: Liam, ETA: 20m with cloud ops).
- If OOM persists: enable soft-fallback to shorter-context summarization flow (engineering quick patch) (owner: Priya, ETA: 1h).

Customer comms (CS script):
- Acknowledge we see increased errors affecting checkouts since 08:12 PT.
- We are in an incident war-room with engineering; immediate mitigations underway.
- ETA for initial mitigation: ~30 minutes; we'll provide 15-min updates until resolved.
- Point of contact: Asha (asha@redwood.ai) and Priya (priya@redwood.ai).

Action items (post-meeting) - short list: (all due times are target, adjust if blocked)
- Mei: Implement seq-length throttle for Helios account and monitor error rate (due 2026-04-15 09:30 PT).
- Jordan: Flip routing to model-variant-B for Helios traffic + validate responses (due 2026-04-15 09:15 PT).
- Liam: Provision burst capacity and watch autoscaler logs (due 2026-04-15 09:40 PT).
- Priya: Create customer-facing update and post to Helios account team + Slack channel (due 2026-04-15 09:20 PT).
- Asha: Coordinate updates, escalate to account exec if customer asks for SLA credits (due 2026-04-15 09:45 PT).
- Mei & Jordan: Capture logs and create minimal reproducer (due 2026-04-15 12:00 PT).

Follow-ups / long-term work (for post-mortem):
- Investigate autoscaler edge-case under burst + add guardrails for scale throttles.
- Improve kernel/quantization compatibility testing for model variants on varying input lengths.
- Add circuit-breaker to detect rapid cache-eviction -> automatically route to stable variant.
- Customer-level rate-limits and per-tenant load shaping recommendations in docs.

Notes to self / discussion points if customer pushes back:
- Be transparent about timeline and what we control (routing, burst capacity).
- Avoid promising root-cause until we have logs; emphasize mitigations and timeframe.
- If customer demands immediate rollback to previous model: ask for safety checks and roll back plan; evaluate risk of older model (owner: Jordan).

Runbook & resources:
- Incident runbook: confluence://runbooks/incident-response
- Autoscaler logs: link in linked_artifacts above (Liam will paste specific log URL in slack).
- Recent deploys: git PR #1245 (model-variant-B tuning) -> keep handy.

Post-meeting deliverables:
- 09:15 initial status update to Helios (Priya + Asha).
- 10:00 incident summary and list of action items + interim RCA (Asha).
- Schedule post-mortem 2026-04-17 10:00 PT (owner: Asha).

Open questions we need answered quickly:
- Do we have evidence of a single model variant being the common factor across OOMs? (measurable: instance id -> variant mapping)
- Can we safely route Helios to variant-B without affecting output quality for their checkout flow? (ask Solutions Eng)
- Is there any cloud provider quota hitting that prevented scale-up? (ask infra)

Quick checklist for war-room start:
- [ ] Slack channel created (incident-helios-checkout) - DONE
- [ ] Invite list: eng-sre, platform, cs, solutions-eng - DONE
- [ ] Customer on a call? - pending (CS to confirm)
- [ ] Initial mitigations implemented (track in meeting) - pending

-- scratchpad notes (raw) --
- customer said "we saw 500s at 8:11" -> keep both times in timeline.
- Prior similar incident Jan 2026 had root cause autoscaler + cache thrash -> check if same pattern.
- Mei thinks seq-length throttle should be safe for checkout (small loss of UX but avoids lost transactions).
- Jordan: model-variant-B has lower mem footprint after recent quantization patch (PR 1245) but slightly higher latency; acceptable trade-off for now.

If anything changes before 09:00 PT, I will update this doc and ping channel.
